annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete 20-page local paper for the missing-tier audit, surveyed every Runge--Kutta construction and order-condition derivation, and compared every candidate with the full frozen Mathlib and NumStability baselines; the previous private neutral check was re-used only for the already isolated easy finite-sum candidate.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P18 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; Journal of Scientific Computing 92, article 6, 2022, pages 1-20

rejected_candidates.reason: These introduce standard Runge--Kutta notation and motivate the mixed-precision midpoint method; the convergence plot is empirical.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the full consistency and perturbation condition lists (3.4) and (3.5) beyond order two
rejected_candidates.reason: The higher-order catalogs require a substantial rooted-tree and differentiability interface, while the smaller order-two subset is finite arithmetic and does not meet T2.

rejected_candidates.candidate: low-precision and naive mixed-precision midpoint error forms in Section 3.2
rejected_candidates.reason: Their O(Δt²)+O(ε) and O(Δt²)+O(εΔt) patterns are earlier, weaker instances whose coefficient equalities are too small for T2.

rejected_candidates.candidate: corrected SDIRK and Lobatto IIIC constructions (4.5) and (4.8)
rejected_candidates.reason: They repeat the correction-order mechanism with larger coefficient arrays but still do not use two substantial NumStability results.
The decimal coefficient tables and stability classifications would require separate exact coefficient certificates and a Runge--Kutta stability interface absent from the frozen library.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Figures 2-6 and their numerical convergence discussions
rejected_candidates.reason: These are finite experiments illustrating the derived asymptotic orders, not universally quantified mathematical results.

rejected_candidates.candidate: stability, efficiency, and varying-epsilon directions in Section 5
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly identifies rigorous stability analysis, efficiency studies, and varying epsilon as limitations or future work rather than completed results.

T1.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. NumStability has no Runge--Kutta or B-series theorem that supplies one substantial step; the source's elementary error split uses only exact subtraction and a triangle inequality.

T2.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. NumStability has no two substantial Runge--Kutta/B-series results, while the corrected-midpoint coefficient equalities themselves are finite arithmetic.

T3.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. A full B-series/order proof could be difficult enough, but the paper does not provide the complete formal derivation needed for a self-contained target. Once its tableau and stability estimates are assumptions, a private neutral proof reduces both global error regimes to a short finite-sum argument below T2 difficulty.

selection_policy: Use accuracy results derived in this paper rather than standard Runge--Kutta definitions, numerical plots, or future-work claims.
Do not replace underspecified asymptotic big-O statements with exact norm inequalities; select exact source content or formalize all asymptotic semantics explicitly.
Preserve the paper's distinction between scheme error, smooth perturbation error, and nonsmooth perturbation error.
Keep every public definition free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source and the compiled condition-L bundle recorded in metadata/library_olean.json.
